 Judgment

This appeal is filed by a concerned State Road Transport Corporation calling in question the judgment and award dated 27.10.2021 in MVC No.1170/2020 on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi [for short, 'the Tribunal'].

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The NC: 2023:KHC-K:1088-DB Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award, has awarded a total sum of Rs.16,44,100/- as compensation to the respondents, who have lost their family member in the road traffic accident involving appellant's bus on 11.11.2022.
2. The first respondent is the husband of the deceased, Smt. Bhimbai, and the other respondents are their children.

There is no dispute about the Tribunal granting compensation of Rs.66,300/-
towards medical bills or Rs.1,20,000/- towards loss of consortium or Rs.30,000/-. towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

The appellant contends that the Tribunal has erred in awarding compensation towards loss of dependency taking the income of the deceased, who was aged 54 years as of the date of accident, in a sum of Rs.14,750/- per month.

sentences.text: Hence, the only question for consideration is whether the loss of dependency must be calculated taking the notional income of the deceased Bhimbai at Rs.14,750/- or any amount lesser than that.

The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the deceased at Rs.14,750/- based on the NC:
2023:KHC-K:1088-DB chart finalized by this Court for settlement in Lok Adalath in the backdrop of the notifications on minimum wages.

4. There could be some controversy on the amount indicated as the monthly notional income for claims arising out of accidents in the year 2020 at Rs.14,750/- as it is contended by the learned counsel for the appellant that though Legal Services Authority indicated Rs.14,750/- at the first instance, but immediately thereafter another letter is issued altering the income for this particular year, and that such altered amount is Rs.13,750/-.
However, the question for the present would be whether this Court must affirm the computation of loss of dependency based on Rs.14,750/-.
5. The deceased Bhimbai was admittedly a home maker and there is no proof of her actual income.

The only assertion about her avocation is that she was engaged in coolie work, and to grant just and reasonable compensation, this Court is of the view that in the present case the loss of dependency must be calculated taking the monthly income NC: 2023:KHC-K:1088-DB at Rs.13,750/- retaining the other parameters viz., multiplier, deduction towards personal expenditure and addition towards future prospects taken by the Tribunal.

If the compensation is recomputed subject to this change,
the respondents would be entitled for compensation under loss of dependency as under:
Computation of Loss of Dependency Description By the Tribunal By this Court Income Rs.14,750.00 Rs.13,750.00 Addition of such Income at the rate 10%
Rs.1,475.00 Rs.1,375.00 towards future prospects Monthly Income with the addition towards Rs.16,225.00 Rs.15,125.00 future prospects

Deduction of 1/3rd towards personal Rs.5408.00 Rs.5,041.00 expenses Monthly income with addition of future Rs.10,817.00 Rs.10,084.00 prospects and deduction towards personal expenses Therefore, Annual Rs.1,29,800.00 Rs.1,21,008.00 Income Loss of Dependency Rs.14,27,800.00 Rs.13,31,088.00 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1088-DB The comparative computation By Tribunal By this Court Description
Loss of dependency Rs.14,27,800.00 Rs.13,31,088.00 Loss of estate & funeral Rs.30,000.00 Rs.30,000.00 expenses Loss of consortium Rs.1,20,000.00 Rs.1,20,000.00
Consequentially, the compensation amount would be Rs.15,47,388/-.

In the light of the afore, the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part modifying the impugned judgment and award dated 27.10.2021 in MVC No.1170/2020 awarding a total sum of Rs.15,47,388/- as compensation.
(ii) The apportionment and disbursement of this amount inter se the respondents shall be as indicated by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal's direction on interest also remains unaltered.
